reasons: The cited paragraphs confirm Section 7 contains only liability caps (7(a)), a consequential-damages waiver (7(b)) and an attorneys'-fee waiver (7(c)); despite the heading 'Indemnification of Contractor' there is no operative defend/indemnify/hold-harmless language, and Section 5(c)'s non-infringement warranty is a warranty, not a defence obligation — so 'missing' is the correct status under the detection guidance.

The inserted 7(d) tracks the model language closely, covering third-party IP infringement, breach of law, Contractor-caused unauthorised disclosure and gross negligence/wilful misconduct, with standard notice, control-with-consent and cooperation mechanics; defined terms are correctly localised ('Works', 'Confidential Information', 'Company').
Placement immediately after the limitation-of-liability provisions matches the redline guidance, and no narrowing of a Customer indemnity is needed because none exists.

The carve-out from Sections 7(a)–(c) is justified rather than over-reaching: without it the fees-paid cap and attorneys'-fee waiver would neutralise the new indemnity, so this is the smallest edit that actually reaches the playbook position.

Comment is accurate, concise, in the required voice, cites the playbook position and offers the fallback (usual IP exclusions and procure/modify/replace/refund remedies). Minor, non-fatal nit: the Section 7 heading ('Indemnification of Contractor') is now inconsistent and could be conformed.
